package_info.package_manager: None (malicious binary distributed via remote download)
package_info.why_malicious: GoTitan is a newly discovered Golang-based botnet distributed via exploitation of CVE-2023-46604 in Apache ActiveMQ. It establishes persistence, collects system information, communicates with a C2 server, and supports multiple DDoS attack methods. Its behavior is fully automated, stealthy, and designed for remote control and abuse.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: It replicates itself as “/.mod” within the system and establishes a recurring execution by registering in the cron. It then retrieves the C2 IP address and gathers essential information about the compromised endpoint, including architecture, memory, and CPU details. Compiling all the collected data using “<==>” as separators, it transmits its collected information to the C2 server. The C2 message initiates with the hard coded string “Titan<==>”.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware copies itself to '/.mod', registers a cron job for persistence, collects system and hardware information, and sends this data to a hardcoded C2 server using a custom protocol.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-replication, unauthorized persistence, and exfiltration of system information to an external server are classic indicators of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate binaries do not replicate themselves to hidden locations, register cron jobs without user consent, or exfiltrate system information.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System management agents may collect and report hardware info, but only to trusted, documented endpoints and with user/admin consent.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of system info to hardcoded C2

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: GoTitan communicates with its C2 server by sending “\xFE\xFE” as a heartbeat signal and waiting for further instructions. When it receives a command, it passes it to a function named “handle_socket_func2” that determines an attack method. GoTitan supports ten different methods of launching distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks: UDP, UDP HEX, TCP, TLS, RAW, HTTP GET, HTTP POST, HTTP HEAD, and HTTP PUT.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware maintains a persistent connection to its C2 server, sends periodic heartbeat signals, receives attack commands, and executes DDoS attacks using multiple protocols.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistent C2 communication, command reception, and DDoS attack execution are hallmarks of botnet malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not maintain unauthorized C2 connections or execute remote-controlled DDoS attacks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may have similar capabilities, but only in controlled, authorized environments.
key_indicators: Support for multiple DDoS attack vectors

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: It replicates itself as “/.mod” within the system and establishes a recurring execution by registering in the cron.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware copies itself to a hidden file and modifies the system's cron configuration to ensure it is executed persistently.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthorized modification of cron for persistence is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not alter cron jobs without explicit user/admin approval.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System maintenance scripts may use cron, but with transparency and user consent.

attack_chain.action: Exploit CVE-2023-46604 to achieve remote code execution on Apache ActiveMQ.
Download and execute GoTitan binary from malicious URL.
Self-replicate as hidden file and register cron job for persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: System information collection and C2 communication

attack_chain.action: Collect system information and exfiltrate to C2 server.
Maintain heartbeat with C2, receive and execute DDoS attack commands.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthorized cron job creation for persistence
Outbound connections to hardcoded C2 IPs with custom protocol markers (e.g., 'Titan<==>', '\xFE\xFE')
Collection and exfiltration of system/hardware information
Execution of multiple DDoS attack methods on remote command
network_indicators: Custom protocol markers in network traffic ('Titan<==>', '\xFE\xFE')
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified hidden binaries (e.g., /.mod), unauthorized cron job entries, and outbound connections to known C2 IPs with custom protocol markers. Look for unusual exfiltration of system information and DDoS attack traffic originating from the host. Correlate with known IOCs and behavioral patterns for Go-based botnets.
